Subject: Private VPC architecture review request — disaggregated control plane

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the earlier walkthrough. We are preparing our internal architecture review for a production on-prem deployment and would like Redwood's take on a disaggregated control plane (control-plane services in customer VPC vs. a managed control plane) and an egress hardening playbook. High level asks:

- Validate the lattice-style control/data plane boundaries for multi-tenant inference clusters (we want strict network demarcation and predictable egress auditability).
- Recommendations for egress flow classification (agent telemetry, model downloads, control commands) and allowable destinations.
- Minimal reference diagrams and a prescriptive playbook we can give ops for cutover.

We're aiming for a design review session next week (Apr 18) and attaching our initial sketch. Can Redwood propose a short checklist and any typical pitfalls?

Hi Liam — appreciate the context and the sketch. Short answers up front: we can support a disaggregated control plane for private deployments if the customer provides a small set of reachable endpoints and outbound-only egress rules; we recommend a lattice-style service boundary (lightweight control-plane proxies in-customer, core orchestration services in a private control plane) to minimize blast radius.

I've sketched a concise playbook and an updated reference diagram and attached both. Proposal: 45-minute design review on Apr 18 at 10:00 PT to walk the diagram and go over egress categories.

Quick bullets of what we'll cover in the review:
- Control plane placement options (fully customer-hosted proxies vs. thin control-plane relay)
- Auth and mTLS trust model for control messages
- Egress classification: telemetry, model fetch, control API, metrics/alerts
- Egress audit and certificate/key rotation procedures
- Cutover checklist and fallbacks (canary deployment of control proxies)

Attachments: vpc-lattice-diagram.png (attachment: vpc-lattice-diagram.png image/png); egress-playbook.md (attachment: egress-playbook.md text/markdown)

On Thu, Apr 12, 2028 at 11:02 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've sketched a concise playbook and an updated reference diagram and attached both.

Adding a couple of security-centric notes before the review so we can be explicit in the session:

- mTLS termination: prefer customer-managed certs at their edge proxy, with Redwood exchanging signed CSRs to avoid keeping long-lived keys in our control plane.
- Least-privilege control channels: control-plane proxies should register only the API surface they need (no broad wildcard scopes). We will provide a small signing token exchange + ephemeral session tokens.
- Egress allowlist pattern: separate 3 categories — model store endpoints (S3 or OCI hosts), telemetry sinks (Splunk/Datadog endpoints), and control/heartbeat endpoints. Each must be whitelisted with CIDR or FQDN + port. Avoid generic 0.0.0.0/0 egress.
- Audit logging: prefer syslog-forwarding to customer's SIEM; we will also emit signed delta logs to Redwood's audit collector for a configurable retention window.

I'll bring sample ACLs and an Excel with recommended rules to the call (attached).

Irene Choi
Lead, Product Security

Thanks everyone. A few operational suggestions I want to call out so the review can focus on tradeoffs:

- Control-plane relay (recommended pattern): lightweight agents in customer VPC maintain outbound-only TLS tunnels to Redwood's control cluster. This keeps inbound firewall rules closed and simplifies NAT traversal.
- Data plane separation: inference workers should not have direct access to control-plane management endpoints; only the relay/proxy can. Use NSGs/security groups to enforce that.
- Caching and model downloads: stage model binaries into an internal, access-controlled mirror to avoid large-scale external egress during rollout.
- Canary cutover: deploy N control proxies, route 5% traffic for 24h, verify metrics and egress logs, then increment. Include an automated fallback route to the previous model variant.

I've updated the diagram to include NAT gateway placement, proxy auto-restart policy, and a sample iptables config for host-based egress enforcement. Attaching updated diagram and a short checklist.
